criteria.semantics: A native whose alt is the image's alt text: what the picture says, in words.

keyboard.outcome: Passes it by: it is not a stop in the tab order.

criteria.name: The image's alt text.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the page's text around the image grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the image scale down to the window's width, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native element.
The image has its alt text, not empty, as the model gives it.
An image is not a control: nothing in it is a stop in the tab order.
WHEN I reach the image with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR its alt text and the role of image, not its file name.
WHEN I swipe to the image with a mobile screen reader (TalkBack, VoiceOver) I HEAR its alt text.

criteria.semantics: The window draws no picture: an image falls back to text, its alt text in fg on bg. Once GPUI draws images and exposes a tree: an AccessKit Image named by its alt text.

keyboard.outcome: Pass the image by: it is no stop of its own; the controls before and after it are.

criteria.name: The image's alt text.

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the alt text grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the alt text drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the alt text at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the alt text drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the alt text whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: I SEE the image's alt text in its place, so what it says is there in words.
WHEN I reach the image's place with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR its alt text.

announce.api: AXImage, its alt text as the AXDescription (AccessKit Role::Image).
ControlType Image, its alt text as the Name.
ATSPI_ROLE_IMAGE, its alt text as the name.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
